CSS

The CSS of a theme

Any CSS: it applies to Desktop Mode only, and wins over the app’s own.

  • Only Desktop Mode. Every rule is put under its root: .rp-card means the cards of Desktop Mode, never the library. :root, html, body and .rp-desk all mean Desktop Mode itself.
  • It wins. Your rules weigh more than the app’s, whatever its selectors: write the selector you mean, nothing more. Only what the app sets on the element itself (an item’s place, a few sizes) needs your !important.
  • Your elements. Every element of a scene is .rp-el.rp-el-<type>, [data-el="its id"], with the classes you give it.
  • The unit. var(--u) is a hundredth of the height of a 16:9 screen as large as the window: calc(var(--u) * 2) looks the same on a TV, a monitor, an ultrawide.
  • Files. url(images/bg.webp) starts from the CSS file’s folder. More files: "styles": ["base.css", "screens.css"].
  • Not allowed. @import and addresses of the network are left out, with a notice.
  • Animations. Any @keyframes; a keyframe with the name of one of the app’s (dk-fade…) takes its place.
  • New CSS. The app runs on a recent Chromium: nesting, :has(), container queries, color-mix(), @property, view transitions.
/* Each section of the bar its own color */
.rp-tab[data-tab='systems'].is-on { color: #7ce7ff; }

/* Nesting works */
.rp-detail {
  .rp-detail-desc { font-size: calc(var(--u) * 2); }
  &[data-system='snes'] .rp-detail-shade { background: linear-gradient(transparent, #2a1a5e); }
}

Good to know

  • Keep effects heavy on the GPU (big blurs, backdrop-filter on every card) for one element at a time: Desktop Mode moves many items.
  • F9 → DevTools opens Chromium’s developer tools: you can try CSS live there, then copy it into your file.
